paragraphs: American Superconductor Corporation (together with its subsidiaries, "AMSC®" or the "Company") was founded on April 9, 1987. At AMSC, we believe that our creativity can meet today's challenges and help us progress to a better future. That means using future-facing technologies to harmonize the world's desire for sustainable progress with the need for more reliable, effective and efficient power delivery. Already, our transformative power solutions are moving the world forward.

We design, develop, and deploy power control solutions that harmonize an increasingly complex energy system, helping our customers scale without added complexity or size. Our system level products leverage the Company's proprietary "smart materials" and "smart software and controls" to provide enhanced resiliency and improved performance of megawatt-scale power flow.

Right now, we are powering the evolution of a grid that is fit for the future: a more reliable and resilient grid built to support and incorporate a broad mix of energy sources. Our pioneering products, software and control solutions are creating more cost-effective and efficient ways to deliver power across a mix of energy sources to ensure a reliable grid that meets the rising demand of power and supports critical infrastructure. This exciting energy future also depends on computer chips, batteries and fuel cells that are built from silicon, lithium and carbon. All of these building blocks must be mined, processed and assembled. Industrial manufacturers of these essential materials as well as semiconductor manufacturers must be able to power their factories in ways that scale without adding complexity or size. Our voltage compensators, capacitors, transformers and rectifiers can power the energy-intensive factories of the future while reducing the risk of costly power interruptions that could hinder this journey to a better future.

In an era of increasing global tensions, we provide advanced power and protection solutions. Our systems help naval vessels reduce magnetic signatures to enhance survivability against magnetically activated threats, while also powering critical onboard systems and supporting shipyard infrastructure. We engineer rugged, compact solutions that protect, power, and perform, so naval fleets stay ready, wherever duty calls.

In the wind power market, we enable manufacturers to field highly competitive wind turbines through our advanced power electronics and control system products, engineering, and support services. Our power grid and wind products and services provide exceptional reliability, security, efficiency, and affordability to our customers.

Our power system solutions help to improve energy efficiency, alleviate power capacity and other constraints, improve system resiliency, and increase the adoption of renewable energy generation. Demand for our solutions is driven by: the growing needs for modernized grids that improve power reliability, security, and quality, the U.S. Navy's effort to upgrade in-board power systems to support fleet electrification, and the need for increased renewable sources of electricity, such as wind and solar energy. Concerns about these factors have led to increased spending by corporations and the military, as well as supportive government regulations and initiatives on local, state and national levels, including renewable portfolio standards, tax incentives, and international treaties. We estimate that the total annual addressable global market for our products and solutions is over $15 billion as of the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026.

Our Company's addressable market is driven by a record global energy transition investment of $2.3 trillion in 2025, up 8% year over year, led by electrified transportation ($893 billion), renewable energy ($690 billion), and grid infrastructure ($483 billion). Approximately $110 billion was recorded in mining and materials investments and $185 billion in semiconductor capacity. These two investments were mostly driven by electrification and energy security, which are accelerating the shift toward stronger domestic supply chains. In addition, we see more than $47 billion of U.S. federal investment in military ship systems and capabilities to help ensure performance and security amid increasing geopolitical uncertainty.

On December 5, 2025, we entered into a Stock Exchange Agreement with the selling stockholders named therein. Pursuant to the terms of the Stock Exchange Agreement and concurrently with entering into such agreement, Mardin Participações Ltda., an entity incorporated in Brazil ("AMSC Brazil") and our wholly-owned subsidiary, directly or indirectly, purchased all of the issued and outstanding shares of Comtrafo Indústria de Transformadores Elétricos S.A. ("Comtrafo"). Comtrafo is a Brazil-based manufacturer of large power and distribution transformers primarily for utility customers and also for industrial customers. Comtrafo is operated and reported as a component of our Grid business segment. We refer to this transaction as the "acquisition of Comtrafo."

On August 1, 2024, we entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement with the selling stockholders named therein. Pursuant to the terms of the Stock Purchase Agreement and concurrently with entering into such agreement, we acquired all of the issued and outstanding shares of Megatran Industries, Inc. Megatran is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company. Megatran's wholly-owned subsidiary, NWL, Inc., ("NWL") is a U.S.-based global producer of engineered power conversion solutions for demanding industrial and military applications. Megatran, together with NWL and its other wholly-owned subsidiaries and affiliates, is operated and reported as a component of our Grid business segment. We refer to this transaction as the "acquisition of NWL."
We provide solutions that address three key drivers of our business: the global demand for traditional and renewable energy;
the global demand for critical materials, including semiconductors, electrification, industrial modernization, and power capacity expansion; and
the electrification of Naval and military capabilities.
This all requires an electric grid that is fit for the future.

paragraphs: Our future financial performance and success are dependent in large part upon our ability to implement our business strategy successfully. Our business strategy envisions several initiatives, including driving revenue growth and enhancing operating results by increasing customer adoption of our products by targeting high-growth segments with commercial and system-level products as well as identifying and completing opportunistic acquisitions. We may not be able to implement our business strategy successfully or achieve the anticipated benefits of our business plan. If we are unable to do so, our long-term growth and profitability may be adversely affected. Even if we are able to implement some or all of the initiatives of our business plan successfully, our operating results may not improve to the extent we anticipate, or at all. In addition, to the extent we have misjudged the nature and extent of industry trends or our competition, we may have difficulty in achieving our strategic objectives. Any failure to implement our business strategy successfully may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. In addition, we may decide to alter or discontinue certain aspects of our business strategy at any time.

Our ability to implement our business strategy could also be affected by a number of factors beyond our control, such as increased competition, legal developments, government regulation, general economic conditions, including as a result of the ongoing wars between Russia and Ukraine and in the Middle East and trade conflicts, or increased operating costs or expenses.
We cannot assure you that we will realize the revenue we expect to generate from our backlog in the periods we expect to realize such revenue, or at all.

In addition, the backlog of orders, if realized, may not result in profitable revenue. Backlog represents the value of contracts and purchase orders received for which delivery is expected in the next twelve months. Our customers have the right under some circumstances and with some penalties or consequences to terminate, reduce or defer firm orders that we have in backlog. In addition, our government contracts are subject to the risks described below. If our customers terminate, reduce or defer firm orders, we may be protected from certain costs and losses, but our sales will nevertheless be adversely affected, and we may not generate the revenue we expect.

Although we strive to maintain ongoing relationships with our customers, there is an ongoing risk that they may cancel orders or reschedule orders due to fluctuations in their business needs or purchasing budgets.

This has had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on our ability to grow our revenues. In addition, current and future suppliers may be less likely to grant us credit, resulting in a negative impact on our working capital and cash flows.

paragraphs: Guided by a belief in the power of next, we are a leading provider of power control solutions that apply innovation and creativity to address today's challenges and enable a more resilient and sustainable energy future. Driven by our purpose "to power progress," we integrate future-facing technologies to balance the growing global demand for power with the need for reliable, and efficient power delivery. Our advanced grid systems, engineering services, power electronics, software controls, and superconductor-based solutions help the traditional and renewable energy sectors, electric utilities, the materials and mining sector, industrial facilities, and other critical infrastructure operators optimize network reliability, improve power quality, alleviate grid constraints, and scale operations without added complexity or size.

We also deliver ship protection and power management solutions that enhance fleet efficiency, survivability, and operational readiness for the U.S. Navy and allied fleets. In the wind power market, we provide advanced electrical control systems, engineering, and support services that help manufacturers lower the cost of wind energy and improve turbine performance. Beyond these markets, we provide industrial process, environmental and emission control capabilities that support operational efficiency across the broader energy infrastructure. Across our businesses, our solutions are helping optimize power networks, strengthen naval capabilities, and support gigawatts of renewable energy generation worldwide as governments and industries continue investing in more resilient, secure, and sustainable power systems.

We operate our business under two market-facing business segments: Grid and Wind. We believe this market centric structure enables us to more effectively anticipate and meet the needs of power generators, power utilities, industrial manufacturers, the military and renewable energy companies.

Grid. Our Grid business segment enables electric utilities, industrial facilities, and traditional and renewable energy project developers to connect, transmit, transform and distribute power with exceptional efficiency, reliability, security and affordability. We provide transmission planning services that allow us to identify power grid congestion, poor power quality, and other risks, which help us determine how our solutions can improve network performance. These services often lead to sales of our grid interconnection solutions for wind farms and solar power plants, power quality systems and transmission and distribution cable systems. We also sell critical shipyard infrastructure power solutions, ship power supplies and ship protection products to U.S. and allied Navies through our Grid business segment.

Wind. Our Wind business segment enables manufacturers to field wind turbines with exceptional power output, reliability and affordability. We supply advanced power electronics and control systems, license our highly engineered wind turbine designs, and provide extensive customer support services to wind turbine manufacturers. Our design portfolio includes a broad range of drivetrains and power ratings of 2 megawatts ("MWs") and higher. We provide a broad range of power electronics and software-based control systems that are highly integrated and designed for optimized performance, efficiency, and grid compatibility.

Our fiscal year begins on April 1 and ends on March 31. When we refer to a particular fiscal year, we are referring to the fiscal year that began on April 1 of that same year. For example, fiscal 2025 refers to the fiscal year that began on April 1, 2025. Other fiscal years follow similarly.

Changes in macroeconomic conditions arising from various reasons, such as the ongoing wars between Russia and Ukraine, and in the Middle East, tariffs, trade restrictions and resulting trade conflicts, labor force availability, sourcing, material delays and global supply chain disruptions could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

On December 5, 2025 (the "Comtrafo Acquisition Date"), we entered into a Stock Exchange Agreement (the "Stock Exchange Agreement") with the selling stockholders named therein. Pursuant to the terms of the Stock Exchange Agreement, Mardin Participações Ltda., an entity incorporated in Brazil ("AMSC Brazil") and our wholly-owned subsidiary, directly or indirectly, purchased all of the issued and outstanding shares of Comtrafo Indústria de Transformadores Elétricos S.A. ("Comtrafo") (the "Comtrafo Acquisition") for (a) (i) 300.0 million Brazilian Real in cash; and (b) 2,417,142 restricted shares of our common stock, $0.01 par value per share (the "AMSC Shares") that were paid and issued, respectively, at closing. In addition, pursuant to certain additional real property agreements, AMSC Brazil through Comtrafo purchased certain real estate assets and transportation assets of Comtrafo for 155.6 million Brazilian Real and 13.4 million Brazilian Real, respectively, in cash. Additionally, AMSC Brazil has agreed to pay the selling stockholders up to an additional 382.5 million Brazilian Real in cash (the "Earnout") upon the achievement of specified earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization ("EBITDA") objectives during the three years following the closing. On May 15, 2026, pursuant to the terms of the Stock Exchange Agreement, Comtrafo purchased a certain real estate asset from the selling stockholders that Comtrafo was leasing and using for administrative and manufacturing operations for 37.2 million Brazilian Real in cash. Comtrafo is a Brazil-based manufacturer of large power and distribution transformers primarily for utility customers and also for industrial customers.

On August 1, 2024, we entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement (the "Stock Purchase Agreement") with the selling stockholders named therein. Pursuant to the terms of the Stock Purchase Agreement and concurrently with entering into such agreement, we acquired all of the issued and outstanding shares of Megatran, Industries, Inc. ("Megatran"), for aggregate consideration in an amount equal to $61.4 million, as may be adjusted pursuant to the Stock Purchase Agreement (the "Purchase Price"), including a cash payment after closing of $5.0 million, as adjusted pursuant to Sections 5.6(c), (d), and (f) of the Stock Purchase Agreement (the "Additional Cash Purchase Price"). At closing, we paid to Megatran's selling stockholders $25.0 million in cash on hand, and 1,297,600 restricted shares of our common stock. On September 23, 2024, we paid the Additional Cash Purchase Price to the selling stockholders, which was calculated based on the agreed upon formula set forth in the Stock Purchase Agreement, in the amount of $8.3 million which includes the Additional Cash Purchase Price and the make whole payment. Megatran's wholly-owned subsidiary, NWL, Inc. (together with Megatran, "NWL"), is a U.S.-based global provider of engineered power conversion solutions for demanding industrial and military applications. As a result of this transaction, Megatran became a wholly-owned subsidiary and is operated by our Grid business segment. We refer to this transaction as the "acquisition of NWL".

paragraphs: American Superconductor Corporation (together with its subsidiaries, "AMSC®" or the "Company") 於 1987 年 4 月 9 日成立。在 AMSC，我們相信我們的創意可以應對當前的挑戰，並幫助我們邁向更美好的未來。這意味著使用面向未來的科技，以調和世界對可持續進步的渴望與對更可靠、更有效率的電力供應的需要。目前，我們的轉型電力解決方案已經在推動世界前進。
我們設計、開發並部署電力控制解決方案，以調和日益複雜的能源系統，幫助客戶在不增加複雜度或規模的情況下擴展業務。我們的系統級產品利用本公司專有的 "智慧材料" 和 "智慧軟體與控制" 技術，以提供提升的韌性與改善的百萬瓦級電力流動表現。

目前，我們正在推動一個適合未來的電網進化：一個更可靠且更具韌性的電網，能夠支持並整合多種能源來源。我們的先驅產品、軟體與控制解決方案正在創造更經濟且高效的電力供應方式，以確保電網的可靠性，並滿足日益增長的電力需求，同時支持關鍵基礎設施。這個令人興奮的能源未來也依賴於由矽、鋰和碳製造的電腦晶片、電池和燃料電池。所有這些構成要素都必須被採礦、加工與組裝。這些關鍵材料的工業製造商以及半導體製造商必須能夠以不增加複雜度或規模的方式來供電其工廠。我們的電壓補償器、電容器、變壓器與整流器可以供應未來能源密集型工廠的電力，同時降低造成高昂電力中斷風險的可能性，這種風險可能會阻礙通往更美好未來的旅程。
在日益升級的全球緊張局勢中，我們提供先進的電力與保護解決方案。我們的系統幫助海軍艦艇降低磁性訊號，以增強對磁性啟動威脅的生存能力，同時也供電於關鍵的艦上系統，並支持船廠基礎設施。我們工程出堅固且緊湊的解決方案，以保護、供電並執行任務，使海軍艦隊隨時準備應對任務需求。
在風力發電市場，我們透過先進的電力電子與控制系統產品、工程與支援服務，協助製造商推出高度競爭的風力渦輪機。我們的電力網與風力產品與服務為客戶提供卓越的可靠性、安全性、效率與經濟性。

我們的電力系統解決方案有助於提高能源效率、緩解電力容量及其他限制、提高系統韌性，並增加可再生能源發電的採用率。對我們解決方案的需求由以下因素驅動：現代化電網日益增長的需求，以提高電力可靠性、安全性與品質；美國海軍努力升級艦載電力系統，以支持艦隊電氣化；以及對增加可再生能源電力來源的需求，例如風能與太陽能。對這些因素的關注已導致企業與軍隊增加支出，以及各層級政府（包括地方、州與國家）的支援性法規與倡議，包括可再生能源組合標準、稅收優惠與國際條約。我們估計，截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日財務年度結束，我們產品與解決方案的總年可達全球市場規模超過 15 十億美元。

我們於 2025 年 12 月 5 日與出售股票股東簽訂股票交易所協議。根據該股票交易所協議的條款，並在簽訂該協議同時，巴西註冊的 Mardin Participações Ltda.（"AMSC Brazil"）及我們的 wholly-owned 子公司，直接或間接購買了 Comtrafo Indústria de Transformadores Elétricos S.A.（"Comtrafo"）所有已發行及流通的股份。Comtrafo 是一家巴西製造大型電力與配電變壓器的公司，主要客戶為電力公司及工業客戶。Comtrafo 由我們的電網業務分部經營並報告為其應報告分部之一。我們將此交易稱為 "收購 Comtrafo"。

2024年8月1日，本公司與名單中所載之出售股東簽訂股票買賣協議。根據股票買賣協議之條款，並與簽訂該協議同時，本公司取得Megatran Industries, Inc.所有已發行及在冊股份。Megatran現為本公司之 wholly-owned subsidiary。Megatran之 wholly-owned subsidiary，NWL, Inc.（"NWL"），為美國境內全球工程電力轉換解決方案之生產商，用於嚴苛之工業與軍事應用。Megatran與NWL及其其他 wholly-owned subsidiaries與 affiliates，作為本公司Grid業務分部之零組件進行營運與報告。本公司將此交易稱為"取得NWL"。
本公司提供解決方案，以應對本公司業務之三大關鍵驅動因素：傳統與可再生能源之全球需求；
關鍵材料之全球需求，包括半導體、電動化、工業現代化與電力容量擴張；以及
海軍與軍事能力之電動化。
此皆需要一個符合未來需求之電力網。

paragraphs: 秉持對未來力量的信念，本公司為提供電力控制解決方案的領導廠商，透過創新與創造力來應對當前的挑戰，並實現更具韌性與永續性的能源未來。我們以「推動進步」為宗旨，整合面向未來的科技，以平衡全球對電力需求的增長與可靠且高效的電力供應需求。我們的先進電網系統、工程服務、電力電子、軟體控制及超導基解決方案，協助傳統與再生能源產業、電力公用事業、材料與礦業、工業設施及其他關鍵基礎設施運營者優化網路可靠性、改善電力品質、緩解電網限制，並在不增加複雜度或規模的情況下擴大運營規模。

我們也提供船舶保護與電力管理解決方案，以提升美國海軍及盟軍艦隊的效率、生存能力與作戰準備度。在風力發電市場，我們提供先進的電氣控制系統、工程與支援服務，協助製造商降低風力發電成本並提升風力渦輪機性能。在這些市場之外，我們提供工業流程、環境與排放控制能力，以支持更廣泛能源基礎設施的運營效率。在各項業務中，我們的解決方案協助優化電力網路、強化海軍能力，並支持全球範圍內數十億瓦特的可再生能源發電，隨著政府與產業持續投資更具韌性、安全與永續的電力系統。
我們的業務運作於兩個面向市場的業務分部：電網與風力。我們認為這種市場導向的結構使我們能更有效地預測並滿足電力發電商、電力公用事業、工業製造商、軍隊與再生能源公司的需求。

電網。我們的電網業務分部協助電力公用事業、工業設施與傳統與再生能源專案開發商，以卓越的效率、可靠性、安全性與經濟性進行電力的連接、傳輸、轉換與分配。我們提供電網規劃服務，使我們能識別電力網的壅塞、電力品質不佳及其他風險，協助我們判斷我們的解決方案如何改善網路表現。這些服務常導致我們銷售電網連接解決方案給風力發電廠與太陽能電廠、電力品質系統與傳輸與配電電纜系統。我們也透過電網業務分部向美國與盟國海軍銷售關鍵船廠基礎設施電力解決方案、船用電力供應與船舶保護產品。
風力。我們的風力業務分部協助製造商推出具備卓越電力輸出、可靠性與經濟性的風力渦輪機。我們提供先進的電力電子與控制系統、授權我們高度工程化的風力渦輪機設計，並為風力渦輪機製造商提供廣泛的客戶支援服務。我們的設計組合包含廣泛的驅動系統與功率等級為 2 兆瓦（"MWs"）及以上的電力等級。我們提供廣泛的電力電子與軟體控制系統，這些系統高度整合，並設計用以實現最佳性能、效率與電網相容性。
我們的會計年度自 4 月 1 日開始，至隔年 3 月 31 日為止。當我們提及特定會計年度時，我們指的是該年度自 4 月 1 日開始的會計年度。例如，財務年度 2025 指的是自 2025 年 4 月 1 日開始的會計年度。其他財務年度依此類推。
總體經濟條件的變化，因各種原因，例如俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間的持續戰爭，以及中東地區的戰爭、關稅、貿易限制及由此產生的貿易衝突、勞動力供應、來源、材料延遲及全球供應鏈中斷，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。

於 2025 年 12 月 5 日（"Comtrafo 收購日"），我們與名單中所列的出售股票股東簽訂了股票交換協議（"股票交換協議"）。根據股票交換協議的條款，巴西註冊的 Mardin Participações Ltda.（"AMSC 巴西"）及我們的 wholly-owned 子公司，直接或間接購買了 Comtrafo Indústria de Transformadores Elétricos S.A.（"Comtrafo"）（"Comtrafo 收購"）所有已發行及流通的股份，總計為（a）（i）300.0 百萬巴西雷亞爾現金；以及（b）2,417,142 限制性股份，每股面值為 0.01 美元（"AMSC 股份"），這些股份在交割時已支付並發行。此外，根據某些額外的實物協議，AMSC 巴西透過 Comtrafo 購買 Comtrafo 的某些實物資產與運輸資產，分別以 155.6 百萬巴西雷亞爾與 13.4 百萬巴西雷亞爾現金支付。此外，AMSC 巴西同意在交割後的三年內達成特定的稅前、稅後、折舊與 amortization（"EBITDA"）目標時，支付至多 382.5 百萬巴西雷亞爾現金（"Earnout"）。於 2026 年 5 月 15 日，根據股票交換協議的條款，Comtrafo 以 37.2 百萬巴西雷亞爾現金從出售股票股東處購入一項實物資產，該資產為 Comtrafo 正在租用並用於行政與製造運營的資產。Comtrafo 是一家巴西公司，主要為電力公用事業及工業客戶製造大型電力與配電變壓器。

於 2024 年 8 月 1 日，本公司與名單中所載之出售股東簽訂股票買賣協議（"股票買賣協議"）。根據股票買賣協議之條款，並同時簽訂該協議，本公司取得 Megatran, Industries, Inc.（"Megatran"）所有已發行及在冊股份，總代價為 61.4 百萬美元，可能根據股票買賣協議進行調整（"購買價格"），包括交割後之現金支付 5.0 百萬美元，根據股票買賣協議第 5.6(c)、(d) 和 (f) 節進行調整（"額外現金購買價格"）。於交割時，本公司以現金支付 25.0 百萬美元予 Megatran 之出售股東，並發放 1,297,600 份限制性普通股。於 2024 年 9 月 23 日，本公司支付額外現金購買價格予出售股東，該額外現金購買價格根據股票買賣協議中所載之協議公式計算，總計為 8.3 百萬美元，包含額外現金購買價格及補償金。Megatran 之 wholly-owned 子公司 NWL, Inc.（與 Megatran 合稱 "NWL"）為美國境內全球提供工程化電力轉換解決方案之供應商，適用於嚴苛之工業與軍事應用。此交易後，Megatran 成為本公司之 wholly-owned 子公司，並由本公司 Grid 事業部經營。本公司將此交易稱為 "取得 NWL"。

headings: 與我們營運相關的風險
若我們未能成功執行業務策略，將可能對財務表現造成損害。
我們可能無法實現所有預期來自訂單與合約的銷售額。
我們依賴第三方供應商提供許多Grid與Wind產品的零組件與次組裝件，使我們面臨供應短缺與價格波動的風險，這可能對業務造成損害。
我們可能取得額外的補充性業務或技術，這可能導致我們產生重大成本，而這些成本可能無法實現預期的效益。
若我們或任何關鍵第三方的資訊科技系統或機密資訊發生故障或遭入侵，將可能對業務與營運造成重大不利影響。
美國政府國防支出的變動可能對財務狀況、營運結果、流動性及整體業務造成負面影響。
若未能遵守不斷演進的資料隱私權與資料保護法規及其他義務，或未能妥善保護個人資料，可能對業務與財務結果造成不利影響。
本公司之成功取決於吸引並留住合資格之人力，若無法做到此點，將可能嚴重影響本公司之業務與前景。
本公司風力發電分部之營業收入有相當大一部分來自單一客戶。若該客戶之業務受到負面影響，將可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司在風力發電市場之成功，取決於取得本公司設計授權之製造商。
許多本公司之營收機會取決於 subcontractors 及其他商業合作夥伴。
本公司前景與財務狀況之不確定性，可能對本公司客戶與供應商關係造成不利影響。
疫情、傳染病或其他公共
對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響
與我們財務表現相關的風險
遞延所得稅資產之計價準備金變動可能影響我們未來的營運成果。
匯率變動可能對我們的營運成果產生負面影響。
我們可能被要求發行履約擔保，此舉將限制我們使用作為擔保品之現金的取得能力。
與我們市場相關的風險
美國與全球經濟狀況之不利變動可能對我們的營運成果產生負面影響。
美國、以色列與伊朗之間持續的衝突已幹擾全球能源市場與供應鏈，並可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響
我們的國際業務面臨我們在美國所不面對的風險，此等風險可能對我們的營運成果產生負面影響。

paragraphs: 本公司未來財務表現與成功，很大程度取決於我們能否成功執行業務策略。本公司業務策略包含多項計畫，包括透過推動營業收入成長與提升營運成果，提高客戶對我們產品的採用率，透過針對高成長性市場段落，以商業與系統層級產品進行目標行銷，以及識別並完成具機會性的併購。我們可能無法成功執行業務策略或達成業務計畫預期的效益。若我們無法做到，將可能對本公司長期成長與獲利造成不利影響。即使我們能成功執行部分或全部業務計畫的計畫，營運成果可能不會如預期般改善，甚至可能完全無法改善。此外，若我們誤判產業趨勢或競爭對手的性質與範圍，我們可能在達成戰略目標上遇到困難。任何未能成功執行業務策略的情況，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成不利影響。此外，本公司可能在任何時間決定改變或終止某些業務策略的方面。
本公司執行業務策略的能力也可能受到一些我們無法控制的因素影響，例如競爭增加、法律發展、政府規範、總體經濟條件，包括因俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間持續的戰爭以及中東地區戰爭與貿易衝突所導致的影響，或營運成本或費用增加。
本公司無法保證我們會在預期期間內實現預期從積壓訂單中產生的收入，甚至可能完全無法實現。
此外，若積壓訂單實現，可能不會產生獲利的收入。積壓訂單代表的是在接獲合約與採購訂單後，預期在未來十二個月內交付的價值。在某些情況下，客戶有權終止、減少或延後我們積壓訂單中的確定訂單，並可能伴隨罰款或後果。此外，本公司政府合約受到下列所描述的風險影響。若客戶終止、減少或延後確定訂單，我們可能對某些成本與損失有所保護，但銷售仍然會受到不利影響，且我們可能無法產生預期的收入。
雖然本公司致力於維持與客戶的長期關係，但客戶可能因業務需求或採購預算的波動而取消或重新排程訂單，這是一項持續存在的風險。
這已對本公司成長營收的能力造成不利影響，且可能持續造成不利影響。此外，目前與未來的供應商可能較不願意給予本公司信用，這將對本公司營運資金與現金流產生負面影響。
